clue.text: Crazy commander's vehicle on isolated piece of land

parts.note: crazy means mad
an aga is a Turkish military commander, here with a possessive
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A deranged officer's car is parked on some remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' looks like it describes the commander, but it is its own piece; the apostrophe in 'commander's' adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is a large island off the coast of Africa, cut off from the mainland by sea.

clue.text: Use roughly later, mat that had been shaken

indicators.note: something shaken has its contents jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doormat is shaken out and later treated roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that had been shaken' rearranges LATER and MAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat someone is to handle them cruelly or harshly.

clue.text: Replacing Dundee strip

indicators.note: replacing the letters means putting them in new places, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A football strip for Dundee is being replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing' rearranges the letters of DUNDEE. Dundee is a Scottish city, and its football clubs wear a strip, the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to lay bare, stripping away a covering.

clue.text: Almost lose sight of mischievous sprite

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: to lose your sight is to go blind

explanation.surface: Someone nearly loses sight of a naughty fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose sight' is the phrase GO BLIND; 'Almost' cuts its final D.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a small, impish creature of folklore that plays tricks.

clue.text: Song about Athens, say

indicators.note: about here signals the letters turned around and jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a song about the city of Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but rearranges the letters of ATHENS and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a work song sung by sailors.

clue.text: Ready with this counter

parts.note: a ready table for working sums is named by putting 'ready' in front of the word for one who counts

explanation.surface: Someone stands prepared with a counter in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A ready reckoner is a printed table of pre-worked calculations; put 'ready' with the answer and you have one.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reckons is one who counts or calculates, a counter.

clue.text: Fixed quickly

explanation.surface: Something was repaired in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast can mean firmly fixed, as in stuck fast, and also at speed.

clue.text: Polished all over

explanation.surface: Everything has been shined from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished means refined or smooth in surface, and also completed or ended.

clue.text: Cavalry unit turned around below square

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumbled part sits below the abbreviation, so it comes after it

parts.note: SQ is the standard abbreviation for square

indicators.note: turned means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troop of horsemen wheels round beneath the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'below' means the jumbled piece comes after the abbreviation; 'turned' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is a cavalry unit of two troops, larger than a troop but smaller than a regiment.

clue.text: Largest vessel aboard — or the most lengthy?

definitions.text: Largest vessel aboard — or the most lengthy?

parts.words: Largest vessel aboard — or the most lengthy?
parts.note: the biggest boat carried by a sailing ship, with a joking second reading as the boat of greatest length

explanation.surface: A question about the biggest small boat carried on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On a sailing ship the longboat was the largest of its boats; the question mark invites the literal reading 'long boat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A longboat is the biggest rowing boat carried by a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Check for any increase in population

definitions.text: Check for any increase in population

parts.words: Check for any increase in population
parts.note: an official count of the people, which shows whether numbers have grown

explanation.surface: Someone monitors whether a population is growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a country's inhabitants, taken to measure its numbers.

clue.text: Rosy giddy in this part of town!

parts.note: rosy means red in colour
giddy can mean light-headed, or simply light

explanation.surface: Someone flushed and dizzy wanders into a seedy district.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark nods to the surface: rosy cheeks and a giddy feeling suit the district named.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-light district is the area of a town where brothels and sex shops cluster.

clue.text: Sidney gets into one position to strike ball legally

indicators.note: gets into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written
Sid is the short form of the name Sidney

explanation.surface: A man called Sidney takes up his stance to hit the ball fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' is the container signal. In cricket the on side (leg side) is a half of the field; in football or rugby an onside player is not illegally ahead of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Being onside means you are in a legal place on the field to play the ball.

clue.text: Soundly recognises the feature

indicators.note: soundly tells us the word is heard, not seen, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to recognise something is to know it

explanation.surface: Someone firmly identifies a characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals a sound-alike of KNOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is one of the features of the face.

clue.text: Mother resents movement outside by director

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap around another piece
movement here means the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother objects to a political campaign being run by a film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is the anagram signal and 'outside' the container signal; 'director' is the definition, as a steersman directs a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A steersman directs the course of a boat, guiding it at the helm.

clue.text: Class of sightseer?

parts.note: a cheap travel class on planes and ships, read as the class a holidaymaker belongs to

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of person goes sightseeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tourist class is the economy section on a plane or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a sightseer, and tourist class is a grade of fare.

clue.text: One expense that's above us

explanation.surface: A single cost is hanging over us.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead is a running business cost, and something overhead is in the sky above.

clue.text: Call on left perhaps of advantageous position

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
left is one example of a side

explanation.surface: A phone call about a left-wing political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts RING above SIDE in this down entry. A ringside seat at a boxing match gives a close view.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside means at the edge of the ring, a close vantage point.

clue.text: One of 13 or 15 in the team to keep at a distance

definitions.text: One of 13 or 15 in the team

explanation.surface: A player chosen from a squad of thirteen or fifteen is told to keep away.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 and 15 are the team sizes in rugby league and rugby union, not entry numbers; the stand-off is the fly-half position in both.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a rugby back position, and to stand off is to keep away or hold aloof.

clue.text: Cycle into explosive weapon

indicators.note: into means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
to cycle is to ride a bicycle

explanation.surface: A bicycle crashes into a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'explosive' looks like an adjective for the weapon but stands for the explosive itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, a weapon of the sea god in myth.

clue.text: Nick followed spinner who is first-rate

indicators.note: followed means the first named piece comes after the second

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a nick is a small cut or notch

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick comes after a spin bowler who is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' poses as a name and 'spinner' as a cricket spin bowler; 'followed' is the order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch means of the very highest quality, excellent.

clue.text: Ancient port might need blowing up!

explanation.surface: An old harbour town may have to be blown up with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' suggests demolition but means inflating with air.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre was a Phoenician port in modern Lebanon, and a flat wheel covering may need inflating.

clue.text: Just, that is to say, shortly becoming member of religious order

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is to say

explanation.surface: Being just, that is, briefly turning into a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges JUST with IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jesuit belongs to the Society of Jesus, a Catholic religious order.

clue.text: Look out when worker admits conflict

indicators.note: admits means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A warning given when an employee confesses to a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like 'confesses' but means BEE lets WAR in.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is a warning to be careful, to watch out.

clue.text: Snap this fiery monster, a bloomer

definitions.text: Snap this fiery monster, a bloomer

parts.words: Snap this fiery monster, a bloomer
parts.note: a fire-breathing beast of legend which, put after the word snap, names a garden flower

explanation.surface: A fire-breathing beast is photographed, though it is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Snapdragon is a garden flower, a bloomer; 'snap' and 'bloomer' (a mistake) suggest a photo gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a legendary fire-breathing monster.

clue.text: Enter referee shortly coming from woody bracken

indicators.note: the letters come out of the clue words in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ref is the short form of referee

explanation.surface: A referee briefly steps out of the undergrowth onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' rearranges ENTER with REF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large fern with a woody trunk, a giant relative of bracken.

clue.text: Middle eastern team having company in the country

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
XI, the Roman eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A side from the Middle East keeps company in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is a team of eleven players, as in cricket or football.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation in North America.

clue.text: A doctor, posh pupil with six-footer, moving about from place to place

definitions.text: moving about from place to place

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
L stands for learner, a pupil driver
an ant is an insect with six feet

explanation.surface: A doctor with a smart pupil and a very tall companion keeps walking around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but is an insect; U is a dated British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambulant describes someone walking or able to walk, travelling about.

clue.text: Had zealously camouflaged tool

indicators.note: camouflaged means concealed in plain view among the letters of the clue words

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly disguised a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camouflaged' signals the run of letters across 'Had zealously'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking tool like an axe with its blade at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Not backbiters

parts.note: biters that are not at the back of the mouth, with a play on the word for slanderers

explanation.surface: People who do not speak ill of others behind their backs.
explanation.walkthrough: A backbiter is a slanderer; read literally, a biter at the back is a molar, so 'not back' biters are at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The incisors at the front of the mouth are the biting teeth, as opposed to molars at the back.
